properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation As of Saturday evening; May 23; 2026: The Santa Rosa Island Fire remains 18;379 acres and is now 87% contained. The additional containment line is from the area of the Water Canyon Campground south towards Skunk Point on the east side of the island. With containment established on the east side of the fire; firefighters and resource advisors worked today on undoing all the efforts of the firefighting efforts in the Main Ranch Complex. Known as suppression-repair; this activity removes potential containment and contingency lines that were put in around the historic structures and assets in the area. Suppression repair also includes the backhauling of equipment such as fire hose that was deployed around the structures; making those supplies available to be transported back to the mainland so they can be refurbished and used on another incident. On the west side of the fire; firefighters are still detecting heat below Soledad Peak and Radar Peak below the Main (Soledad) Road. Tomorrow; fire crews will go directly into the area where the heat is being detected. While the area has fireline around it; as part of the process; firefighters are methodically checking that line before calling it contained. Additionally; as the fire containment increases; some fire crews are getting the opportunity to return home; while other crews will be coming in with specialty skills in fighting fire in this complex environment. This explains why the number of personnel increased today; when this transition happens; current firefighters assigned share their information and knowledge with the incoming crews to ensure common operating pictures; safety plans; and situational awareness are known by all. This tactic of overlapping crews is commonly referred to as “shadowing” ensuring consistence coverage. This will be the final evening update for the Santa Rosa Island Fire unless significant activity occurs. Background: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Closures: Santa Rosa Island is closed to all day and overnight use through at least June 6; 2026; due to the wildfire. All Water Canyon Campground reservations have been cancelled through this date and visitors have been notified by email. Campground reservation holders with bookings through August 14; 2026; have also been informed that the wildfire may affect their stay. If additional cancellations are needed; they will receive follow-up emails. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed; along with a wind shelter at a campsite at Water Canyon Campground. Weather: Cool and moist conditions will continue for the next few days as the marine layer remains deep and onshore flow prevails. The typical west to northwest winds will begin to increase on Sunday afternoon/evening; with further increase in speed and coverage on Monday.
